title: Two arrested after break-in at country home of Prince William and wife Kate, UK police say | CNN
text:
Source: Reuters

Two men have been arrested on suspicion of burglary and trespass after a break-in at the country residence of Britain’sPrince Williamand his wife Kate, British police said on Tuesday.

Norfolk Constabulary said police were called on Monday night following a report of suspicious activity at a property on the royal family’s Sandringham estate in Norfolk, eastern England. The property was unoccupied at the time, police added.

The Sun newspaper first reported that police were investigating a break-in at Anmer Hall, a 10-bedroom house which the late Queen Elizabeth II gave William and Kate as a wedding present in 2011.

Although they use the country retreat for holidays and short breaks, their main home is on the Windsor Castle estate to the west of London.

A spokesperson for William said they did not comment on security matters.

The news came as William visited Prime Minister Andy Burnham at the British leader’s office, 10 Downing Street.

While the British royals often mingle with political leaders and government ministers at formal occasions, visits to Downing Street, the official residence of British leaders since 1735, are more infrequent.

The late Queen dined with Winston Churchill at “Number 10” in 1955 on the eve of his resignation and became the first monarch for possibly 200 years to attend a Cabinet meeting there in 2012 during her Diamond Jubilee year.

As heir, King Charles also made a number of trips to Downing Street to attend meetings and see how the government functioned, while William’s late mother Diana, Princess of Wales also visited almost exactly 37 years ago in 1989.
